title: Anchor stored memory timestamps canonically instead of baking deictic relative times into prose

sections.what: Stop baking deictic relative phrases (such as earlier today, six hours ago, or just now) into persisted memory prose and reflection summaries; store canonical world-time anchors (tick and day/clock metadata) and let tickToRelative() render the single live relative prefix at prompt-assembly time.
sections.why: Observed during Millwood/fieldhouse memory analysis: a memory stored at tick T with baked-in prose ('[6 days ago] Earlier today (8:00 AM, bus): On the school bus six hours ago...') collides with memory-context.ts prepending tickToRelative(mem.tick). Days or weeks later, Actor and Intermediator see four contradictory timeframes in one line, corrupting causal ordering and temporal reasoning.
sections.how:
1. Audit static/js/agent/memory-manager.ts, reflection/summarization prompts, and engine/agent_memory.py write paths so generated or stored memory text uses absolute in-world clock/day anchors (for example Day 12, 08:00, school bus) and excludes fleeting deictic adverbs from persisted mem.text.
2. Update static/js/agent/prompt-builder/memory-context.ts (lines 323, 364, 382 where tickToRelative(mem.tick) is prepended) so relative offset labels are rendered once from (currentTick - mem.tick) alongside optional compact wall-clock metadata without colliding with body text.
3. Add a prompt/normalization guard for Memory Intermediator (task-948) and reflection summaries so consolidated memories preserve source tick spans rather than freezing transient relative words into persistent palimpsest prose.
sections.verify:
1. Create or reflect a memory at morning tick T and format I REMEMBER at T+6h, T+6d, and T+35d.
2. Verify the rendered line contains one consistent dynamic age prefix ([6 hours ago], [6 days ago], [5 weeks ago]) plus canonical event time/location, with zero conflicting Earlier today / six hours ago leftovers inside mem.text.

acceptance.text: Memory creation, reflection, and Intermediator summarization prompts forbid baking deictic relative phrases ('today', 'earlier today', 'just now', 'N hours ago') into stored memory prose and anchor events by world tick/clock time instead.
memory-context.ts renders [relative] dynamically from currentTick - mem.tick (plus optional absolute day/clock tag) without producing conflicting dual-timeframe strings even weeks after encoding.
Unit tests cover multi-day and multi-week recall rendering (same-day, +6d, +35d) asserting no contradictory relative time phrases remain in assembled memory lines.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Mind Panel Memory tab (static/js/inspector/) and Prompt Preview debug view.

Current availability: Existing Memory Inspector displays stored mem.text and tick metadata; memory-context.ts dynamically prepends tickToRelative(mem.tick) at prompt build time.

Manual verification steps:
1. Author or trigger a morning conversation memory at tick T, then advance world time by 6 hours and by 6 days.
2. Inspect the character's Mind Panel Memory list and Prompt Preview I REMEMBER section.
   - expected: Stored prose uses stable clock/location anchors (for example 08:00, school bus), while only the dynamic prefix updates from [6 hours ago] to [6 days ago].
